$comment: The identity of the bun this repo builds with, declared once because the
version STRING cannot carry it.
THE PROBLEM, measured 2026-08-16. bun 1.4 is not released. It is not on npm
in any form: the registry's newest bun is 1.3.14 (2026-05-13) and its
`canary` dist-tag points at a 1.3.13 canary. The 1.4 line exists only as a
GitHub release asset under the tag `canary`, and THAT TAG ROLLS — the
darwin-aarch64 asset reported updated_at 2026-08-16T11:26:46Z while the
release itself is titled after a different commit than the binary reports.
There is no immutable per-canary tag (bun-v1.4.0-canary.1 answers 404).
So `1.4.0-canary.1` names a MOVING TARGET. package.json's packageManager
field holds that string and looks like a pin; it is a label that will stay
constant while the binary under it changes daily. Pinning by version here
would be the same class of mistake as trusting a flag --help omits.
WHAT IS PINNED INSTEAD is the binary's SHA-256, plus the capability the
repo actually depends on. check-bun-canary.mjs asserts both. When bun rolls
the canary the sha stops matching and CI goes red by name, which is the
point: a bump becomes a deliberate, visible commit rather than a silent
change of compiler underneath a content-addressed artifact graph.
THE CAPABILITY is not a preference. bun 1.3.14 accepts zstdCompressSync's
`dictionary` option and silently ignores it (measured: none=65 good=65
wrong=65, against node's 65/18/64), which ships no-op dcz deltas — gotcha
28. build.mjs feature-detects it and throws, but 40 seconds into a build.
The probe below is the same control run first and named.
Re-verify with: bun run bun:canary:check

verified.zstd_dictionary: none=65 good=18 wrong=64 (honours it, same as node v26.7.0)
